#828. It’s Happy Harry Kane day as England’s finest seizes his moment in style | Barney Ronay

The Ballon d’Or validated the forward’s career and he extended his incredible record for England with yet another goal on his 126th appearance

Happy Harry Kane day! And many happy Harry returns. There is a process in clinical psychology known as semantic satiation. Subjects are asked to repeat a word or phrase so many times that it loses any kind of meaning. Suddenly “daffodils” is just an absurd, empty set of sounds. So it was in the buildup to Harry Kane’s record-breaking 126th cap, at the end of Harry Kane Ballon d’Or fortnight, as Harry Kane’s England were led out by top scorer Harry Kane, climax to a week of Harry Kane tributes, Harry Kane montages, 26-page Harry Kane … wait. Where were we?

This was that kind of occasion from start to finish, a night where you expected to look up from your desk mid-match to see Kane’s head looming helpfully over your shoulder, to enter the Wembley toilets at half-time and find him silently offering you a breath mint and a scented tissue.

Football loves its rankings and ratings. England loves a formal march-past. The Harry Kane moment was always going to come at Wembley. And it duly arrived with 61 minutes gone and the score 1-1 in a meandering game of mid-November England product.

There may be less satisfying ways to decide a game of football than a VAR-screen penalty awarded for an overly prolonged grab of the collar on a player who wasn’t going to get the ball. But it’s hard to think of many right now.

It was enough here. There was a gathering roar from the Wembley crowd, luxuriating in the prospect of a Kane penalty sequence: the pre-kick close-up, the jaw, the stare, the iconic hairline. Kane delivered, rolling the ball into the centre of the goal. There was a leap, a punch of the air, an embrace in front of a billowing George Cross flag.

At times like these it is hard to remember a time when Kane wasn’t exactly here doing exactly this, to accept that he won’t just be out there doing it for ever. Although the good news is he now gets to re-break the caps record every time he plays, thereby ensuring more ceremony, more pomp, more of that sweet, sweet, neural fatigue.

No doubt the haters will say: typical Kane. A low-key Wembley. A cheapish penalty kick. The numbers ticking over. But that’s the haters for you, as relentless in their own way as Kane himself. The goal made it 92 in 126 games, which really is mind-boggling in its focus and longevity, the sheer will to keep doing this. Imagine not thinking Kane is England’s best player since Bobby Charlton. What else are you supposed to do out there?

Wembley had been cold and crisp at kick-off, gripped with the familiar echoey, midweek chill, the booming PA, the thin air, like being present at a vast corporate presentation or the opening of a mega-sale in the world’s largest out-of-town DIY warehouse.

The military personnel wobbled the massive flag. Tongues of fire leapt around the perimeter. And as the teams lined up there was a surprise appearance from the real star of this stage, the Ballon d’Or itself, wreathed in event glamour and star-flash.

Kane drew the ballon from its stone in Arthurian fashion, then held it a little sheepishly in one hand. Prince William walked out and gave him a massive framed shirt, which seemed weird in the moment, like the chief area sales manager presenting the prize from the Christmas raffle. Has Prince William ever been asked to carry anything before?

A little earlier a vast Harry Kane tifo had appeared at one end, showing Kane in full roaring lion mode. It carried the tagline “England’s finest”, which sounds like a type of cheddar cheese you can buy at the airport gift shop. But it’s also a good compromise. He is indeed very fine.

It was a striking coronation for a player who made his debut here 11 years ago as a promising other-guy under Roy Hodgson. There is still a similar element of double-take about that Ballon d’Or. Kane has always seemed like one of those sports people destined to be reaching for something, constantly in search of a final validation. This has been his strength and his energy. Well, we’re here now. Kane has his notch on the forever tree. Ultimacy arrived on a London stage dressed in a shiny tuxedo.

This does change something. Kane’s entire professional life is now divided into two parts. Everything up to 26 October 2026. And then the last 17 days. How does it feel now? Is the air pressure different, the noise in his head, the tension in his ears?

Here the whole team started slowly. In the opening four and a half minutes Croatia had 92 per cent possession and England made one pass. Thomas Tuchel was up early in his puffy winter coat, tight black slacks and black business shoes, like an actuary going sledging. Kane lurked in some strange deep position and played one or two overambitious passes.

Is this something new? Arrogant Kane. Big-shot Kane. Has he become our Ronaldo? Maybe he should have angrily retired straight after the game and promised to speak his truth on a YouTube chatshow.

Instead Kane helped to make the opening goal for Morgan Rogers, set up with a lovely floated diagonal pass and an expert cutback from Jude Bellingham. England faded a little and were pegged back around the hour. Lewis Hall played well. Trent Alexander-Arnold was fun to watch. They have now definitively qualified for the Nations League knockouts, which is certainly a thing. But in the end this was always going to be Harry’s day.

From six minutes of darkness in Egypt or totality over the Australian Outback, here are the pros and cons of the next two total solar eclipses.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

For those who want to experience a total solar eclipse, the next two years present the best kind of problem. On Aug. 2, 2027, the so-called "eclipse of the century" will sweep across southern Spain, North Africa and the Middle East, bringing more than six minutes of totality to parts of Egypt. Then, on July 22, 2028, another exceptionally long total solar eclipse will cross Australia, putting the remote Outback and Sydney Harbor in the path of the moon's dark central shadow before it reaches New Zealand's beautiful South Island.

Both eclipses will be spectacular, and both will require careful planning, yet they promise very different experiences. The 2027 event combines over six minutes of totality with some of the very best weather prospects possible, while 2028 offers over five minutes of totality above some of the world's most famous wildernesses and cityscapes.

Eclipse chasing requires careful planning and dedication, but also significant funds. If you can only choose one, which should it be?

On paper, 2027 is difficult to beat. Maximum totality on Aug. 2 will last about 6 minutes, 23 seconds, making it the longest totality on land since 1991 and until 2114. The path of totality will cross southern Spain and Gibraltar before sweeping across Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt, Sudan, Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Somalia and the Chagos Islands. About 88.9 million people live in its path, according to Time and Date. It will dominate the news for weeks.

For Europeans, southern Spain is the obvious easy option. Tarifa, at the country's southern tip, will see about 4 minutes, 39 seconds of totality, while the U.K. Overseas Territory of Gibraltar gets about 4 minutes, 25 seconds. Travel farther east and the duration increases, with Sfax in Tunisia getting around 5 minutes, 41 seconds and locations in Egypt experiencing more than six minutes. Weather prospects generally improve, too, as the path crosses the deserts of North Africa.

Egypt is the headline destination. Luxor will see about 6 minutes, 20 seconds of totality near midday, with Karnak Temple, the Valley of the Kings, and some of the world's greatest ancient monuments nearby. The climatic odds are excellent, with clouds extremely rare in early August. That combination of a very long totality, ancient landscapes and a very high probability of a clear sky makes 2027's path of totality highly unusual.

But there are downsides. Temperatures around Luxor can exceed 105°F (41°C) in August, a dust storm is not impossible, and totality occurs shortly after 1 p.m. when the sun (and moon) will be high overhead — making photography very difficult. Demand is already intense, making organized trips expensive. Spain will be considerably easier and probably cheaper for European eclipse chasers, but at the expense of roughly two minutes of totality — and slightly less favorable weather prospects.

If 2027 is about extreme duration, 2028 is about choice. On July 22, 2028, a path of totality will cross the Cocos Islands, Christmas Island, Australia, from northwest to southeast — passing directly over Sydney — before continuing across the Tasman Sea to New Zealand's South Island. That's about 6.3 million people, according to Time and Date. This will be an exclusive eclipse experienced by relatively few people, certainly when compared to the eclipses in 2024, 2026 and 2027.

Maximum totality will last 5 minutes and 10 seconds in the remote Kimberley region of Western Australia. That's more than a minute shorter than 2027, but still exceptionally long by total solar eclipse standards (most last about two minutes). More importantly, the Australian Outback has excellent climatic prospects. Historical cloudiness on July 22 is around 8% at Purnululu (Bungle Bungles) close to the point of greatest eclipse in Western Australia and 19% at Karlu Karlu (Devil's Marbles) in the Northern Territory, making Australia's interior an attractive destination for serious eclipse chasers. Temperatures will be around 86°F (30°C) in July.

Then there's Sydney. Australia's largest city will experience about 3 minutes, 45 seconds of totality, its first total solar eclipse since 1857. Sydney Opera House and Harbor Bridge beneath a totally eclipsed sun could produce some of the decade's defining astronomical images, while millions of people experiencing totality together should create an extraordinary atmosphere. Temperatures will be around 62.6°F (17°C).

A compromise is weather. Historical cloudiness in Sydney is around 43%, which is good odds for most eclipses — and July is known for clear weather. But in 2028, anyone prioritizing their chances of a clear totality will be tempted by a (albeit pricier) trip to the Outback. For Europeans, reaching Australia also comes with considerable cost and time. The huge number of hotels in Sydney could keep accommodation relatively competitive, but the long flight means it makes little sense to travel there for only a few days. For many international eclipse chasers, 2028 will naturally become an expensive one- or two-week trip.

There's another reason to think beyond those few minutes of darkness. With the right planning, an eclipse trip can also become an extraordinary astronomy vacation (tip: come a week before the eclipse for the darkest evening skies). Here, 2028 offers visitors from Europe and North America something very different — the Southern Hemisphere night sky.

July is a superb time to see the bright central regions of the Milky Way from dark locations in Australia. The Southern Cross, or Crux, is one of the southern sky's defining sights, with Alpha and Beta Centauri nearby. Omega Centauri, the largest and brightest globular cluster visible from Earth, is another showpiece, while the Eta Carinae region offers one of the richest sections of the Milky Way for binoculars and small telescopes.

There are other reasons to extend the trip. A partial lunar eclipse occurs on July 6-7, 2028, while the Southern Delta Aquariid meteor shower peaks around July 28 — a week after the eclipse, during a first-quarter moon — and is particularly well seen from the Southern Hemisphere. Add Australia's world-class dark skies, and a trip into the Outback could become as much about stargazing as the eclipse itself.

The 2027 eclipse has fewer night-sky extras. The Delta Aquariid meteor shower peaks a few days before the eclipse — in dark, moonless skies — while Jupiter will dominate the western sky shortly after sunset. However, anyone traveling from the Northern Hemisphere will largely see a familiar celestial hemisphere. Australia offers a genuinely different sky experience.

Perhaps the most useful way to choose between these eclipses is not to compare their durations, but to imagine where you would most like to be when the moon's shadow arrives.

In 2027, the decision largely comes down to how far along the eclipse track you want to travel. Stay in southern Spain for convenience and around four minutes of totality, head into Tunisia for longer totality and excellent weather prospects, or go all-in on Egypt for more than six minutes beneath almost cloudless desert skies — and bragging rights among eclipse chasers. It's an eclipse that can be combined with beaches, Roman ruins, North African cities or the temples and, of course, the tombs of ancient Egypt.

In 2028, the contrast is even greater. Sydney offers a communal total solar eclipse — a busy "we eclipse" — with millions watching daylight disappear above one of the world's great cities. Head thousands of miles away into the Australian interior and the same event becomes a lonely "me eclipse" in the wilderness, with up to five minutes of totality above an immense Outback landscape. Continue to New Zealand, and there's yet another possibility — a shorter totality with the sun much lower in the afternoon sky.

If your priority is purely totality duration, 2027 marginally wins. More than six minutes of totality combined with extraordinarily reliable weather is a rare combination. There's a good reason Aug. 2, 2027 is being marketed as the "eclipse of the century." But if you've always wanted to visit Australia or New Zealand, the 2028 eclipse is an extraordinary excuse to finally go, in addition to experiencing a long totality.

Choose the trip you most want to take, then find the best possible place for you within the path of totality. After all, no total solar eclipse lasts long enough, and most eclipse chasers struggle to recall exactly how long totality lasted. They're just left with the same question as always — when is the next one?

Jamie is an experienced science and travel journalist, stargazer and eclipse chaser who writes about exploring the night sky, solar and lunar eclipses, the Northern Lights, moon-gazing, astro-travel, astronomy and space exploration. He is the editor of WhenIsTheNextEclipse.com, author of A Stargazing Program For Beginners, co-author of The Eclipse Effect, and a senior contributor at Forbes.

#826. Gritty Arsenal show different side in Barcelona draw

Arsenal secure crucial draw against wasteful Barcelona in Champions League

It is no mean feat for any team to come away from Camp Nou with a result against Barcelona in the Women's Champions League, let alone a side struggling for form.

With that context in mind, Arsenal's draw on Thursday night was a significant achievement and increases their chances of qualifying for the knockout stages of the competition.

Sitting sixth in the Women's Super League table, their title hopes in tatters, Renee Slegers' side are putting all their eggs in one basket and hoping for success in Europe.

They have a promising seven points from their opening four matches and while giants Lyon await in London next week, their draw with Barca could provide a welcome boost.

Arsenal secure gutsy Champions League draw at Barcelona

Arsenal defender Steph Catley made five interceptions and nine clearances at Camp Nou to deny Barcelona

It was not a scintillating display from Arsenal, nor a tactical masterclass, but it was a gritty showing that we have not seen enough of this season.

With manager Slegers under scrutiny and the players under pressure to perform, the last thing they needed was to face the full-throttle Barcelona attack.

Caroline Graham Hansen's cleverness, Sydney Schertenleib's constant threat and the aura of top scorer Ewa Pajor is enough to strike fear into any team in Europe.

Even with three-time Ballon d'Or winner Aitana Bonmati on the bench, Barcelona were able to impose their superiority against a wounded Arsenal â but the Gunners stood firm.

Frida Maanum opened the scoring against the run of play for Arsenal in the first half and they somehow made it to half-time with their lead intact despite 18 shots from their dominant hosts.

Barcelona did continue as expected after the break, equalising through Graham Hansen, but failed to kick on, with Arsenal's experience and maturity showing to see out a draw that ended the Catalan giants' 100% record in this season's Champions League.

"I'm very pleased in general with the players and how they have gone about it, their preparation, ownership and engagement. You know in these games it's about the margins," said Slegers.

"The execution was so good. It is always going to be difficult against Barcelona because they are so good on the ball. It's hard to defend against but we did well.

"We knew there would be opportunities. I'm really pleased with the way we played as it's very different to how we usually play. That we can do it this way [is] a big boost for us as a team.

"We will take that going forward because the next games are coming quickly. It is really difficult to go to Camp Nou. The one point is okay for us, though obviously we went for three."

Criticism of Arsenal this season has centred around their lack of ruthlessness and an inability to turn dominance into winning results.

The tables turned on Thursday as it was Barcelona who were wasteful and frustrating, while Arsenal rode their luck and capitalised where they could.

Defending champions Barcelona had almost 70% possession, 24 shots, 51 touches inside the opposition half and 11 corners but only managed the solitary goal.

Slegers admitted on Tuesday "too many draws" had impacted their start to the season â but was this particular draw proof that the real Arsenal is still hidden among the low confidence and poor form?

"This is a very different game to play but there are of course elements in the performance that we want - and need - to take forward," added Slegers.

"It's there in the team and we need to show that in every single game. If you ask me what words I would use to describe the performance, I would say grit, resilience, clarity, discipline, communication, leadership and bravery as well.

"That is a lot of words but there were a lot of really good things in this performance that we definitely want to build on."

It is a decisive few days for Arsenal with high-flying London City Lionesses up next on Sunday for a game that could impact their hopes of qualifying for next season's Champions League in the battle for a top three spot in the WSL.

Then, they host French giants Lyon in Europe next Thursday before ending the league phase at Inter Milan in December.

#825. Why Fans Think Usher Is Feuding With Chris Brown Amid Joint Tour

Usher and Chris Brown sparked feud rumors after canceling six shows in their joint The R&B: Raymond & Brown Tour, which kicked off in June.

Usher and Chris Brown may be caught up in some drama.

The singers are sparking rumors of a behind-the-scenes feud after canceling six shows—all of which were added to the touring schedule three months ago—in their ongoing The R&B: Raymond & Brown Tour, which initially kicked off in June.

The first sting of cancellations came in October, with shows in Baltimore, Cincinnati, Indianapolis and Columbia, S.C., affected. At the time, organizers said the concerts were axed to "prioritize the health and well-being of the touring party and crew."

"The demands of a tour of this length and scale are significant," they said in a statement to Complex, "and these adjustments will allow the tour to continue safely and sustainably through the remaining scheduled performances."

However, two more concerts were canceled on Nov. 10, less than one week after Usher and Brown's show in Atlanta was pushed back by nearly three hours, according to TMZ.

Between the delay and the mass cancellations, many are starting to believe that Usher and Brown got it bad.

"Two of the smoothest men in R&B history. Can't agree on a start time," one fan wrote on X, while another quipped, "This usher Chris brown thing im ctfu."

Still, the duo put on a united front on Nov. 10 during the fourth night of their five-show stop in Atlanta, with Brown, 37, calling the Grammy winner his "brother" in concert videos posted on social media.

E! News has reached out to Usher and Brown's reps for comment but hasn't heard back.

Usher, 48, and Brown are now only slated to perform at Los Angeles' SoFi Stadium Nov. 15 after canceling their Nov. 16 show at the arena. They are also due to make stops in New Orleans, Houston and Miami—which saw its three-show lineup downgraded to two—before wrapping up the tour in Tampa Dec. 12.

As the two continue to run it with their tour, read on for more details about Hollywood's biggest feuds.

The Sex and the City costars had dodged feud rumors for years, but they were reignited after Cattrall decided not to return for a third movie and made comments about her SLP that raised eyebrows.

"What was your reaction to Kim Cattrall telling Piers Morgan that you were never friends just colleagues?" Andy Cohen asked Parker on a September 2017 episode of Watch What Happens Live.

As she explained, "Just...heartbroken. I mean that whole week, you and I spoke about it because I was just...I don't know I found it really upsetting because that's, you know, that's not the way I recall our experience."

"So...it's sad but I'm kind of...I don't know, I always think that what ties us together is this singular experience is the thing," she continued. "It was a professional experience but it became personal because it was years and years of our lives. So I'm hoping that that sort of eclipses anything that's been recently spoken. That many years spent doing something so special that people had a connection with is such a privileged."

And though they didn't film scenes together, Cattrall did make a small appearance on And Just Like That.

During a 2022 TikTok challenge, JoJo Siwa described Candace Cameron Bure as the "rudest" celebrity, later explaining that she felt snubbed when Bure once refused to take a picture with her on a red carpet. Shortly after the dig, however, the Full House alum apologized: "I kind of broke your 11-year-old heart. I didn't take a picture with you. Ugh! I feel crummy, I feel—JoJo, I'm so sorry."

The two made amends. But months later, Cameron Bure was asked if she expects the Great American Family network, of which she serves as chief creative officer, to feature same-sex couples as leads in holiday movies. She said no, adding, "I think that Great American Family will keep traditional marriage at the core."

Siwa, who came out as a member of the LGBTQ+ community in 2021, wrote on Instagram that the actress' comment is "rude and hurtful to a whole community of people."

In August 2022, Morris and Pope traded harsh words with Aldean, wife of fellow country star Jason Aldean, after she shared an Instagram Reel of herself applying makeup, writing, "I'd really like to thank my parents for not changing my gender when I went through my tomboy phase. I love this girly life."

Berk (pictured second from left) addressed rumors of a falling out with France (middle) in January 2024, two months after he announced his exit from Queer Eye after eight seasons.

"I want people to know that Tan and I—we will be fine," he told Vanity Fair. "There was a situation, and that's between Tan and I, and it has nothing to do with the show. It was something personal that had been brewing—and nothing romantic, just to clarify that."

In March 2024, France responded to allegations that he had campaigned to replace Berk on Queer Eye with his friend Jeremiah Brent.

"Netflix and the production companies did a full-on casting. I didn't put my friend up for the job. They ended up getting it because they were the best person for the job," he said on Instagram. "But I didn't get them hired by getting rid of somebody else."

In September 2023, while playing a game called Stir the Pot with her daughter Kelly Osbourne on E! News, Sharon said the That '70s Show alum was the rudest celebrity she had ever met, branding him, a "rude, rude, rude, rude little boy" and a "dastardly little thing."

He did not respond to her remarks publicly.

Five years prior, Sharon told Larry King that when Ashton appeared on The Talk in 2014, he had an "attitude" after she got his name wrong.

"He goes, 'What are you, what have you done in this industry?'" she recalled. "And I was like, 'Kid, don't start with me, because I'm gonna eat you up and s--t you out.' So I was just like, 'You don't know what you're dealing with, kid.'"

Back in June 2021, the Hole frontwoman accused Rodrigo of copying her band's album cover for a promotional photo without giving credit, prompting the Disney alum to respond, "Love u and live through this sooooo much."

however, it seemed their hatchet was buried when Love replied, "Olivia - you're welcome. My favorite florist is in Notting Hill, London! Dm me for deets! I look forward to reading your note [winking face emoji]."

During a 2019 appearance on Watch What Happens Live, the Happy Days actor was asked why he didn't get along with the Forrest Gump star on the set of the 1989 flick Turner & Hooch.

"I was directing that movie for 13 days," Winkler recalled, "and then I was called into [producer] Jeff Katzenberg's office and he said, 'You have everything with you? Go home.'"

He did, however, seem to get along with Hanks' four-legged costar, quipping, "Love that dog."

Winkler later denied speculation that he still had beef with the Oscar winner, telling TMZ in 2020, "I don't have a feud with Tom Hanks."

Fans of The Hills will remember that iconic line, delivered by Conrad on the season three premiere. Their feud began when Montag started dating her now-husband Spencer Pratt, and hit its peak when Conrad accused her and Pratt of starting a rumor that she had made a sex tape with then-boyfriend Jason Wahler.

The costars reignited their ongoing feud in 2017 when Gibson publicly called out Johnson on Instagram after the Fast and Furious 9 release date was pushed back to April 2020. That same day, it was announced that a Fast and Furious spinoff starring Johnson and Jason Statham would hit theaters in 2019. The following month, Gibson threatened to quit Fast 9 if Johnson was in the movie.

Gibson then opened up about the feud, telling Van Lathan on The Red Pill podcast, "I have yet to talk to The Rock to this day, and we will have a conversation." He shared that he did have a chat with the former wrestler's producing partner, but not the actor himself.

"I found myself being the messenger on behalf of various people associated to the franchise, but stupid me was the only one who went public about those feelings, which is my own fault," gibson said. "It's not professional, it's not cool."

Swift and Perry had been in a feud for years, with their rift even allegedly inspiring the former's song "Bad Blood." The drama, which reportedly started over a backup dancer and competing tours, came to an end after Perry sent Swift a literal olive branch before her Reputation Tour kickoff in 2018.

"So I just got to my dressing room and found this actual olive branch," Swift said in an Instagram video. "This mean so much."

She captioned the video, "Thank you Katy."

The iconic singers have been feuding since 2004. While accepting the Classic Songwriter Award at the Q Awards that year, John said to attendees, "Madonna, best f--king live act? F--k off! Since when has lip-syncing been live? Sorry about that, but I think everyone who lip-syncs in public on stage, when you pay like 75 quid to see them, should be shot."

The former Grey's Anatomy star sparked a feud with the series creator in 2008 when she removed her name from the Emmy Awards consideration. Heigl stated that her reason for the move was because she wasn't "given the material to warrant a nomination."

Rhimes later opened up about Heigl's decision during an interview with Oprah Winfrey on Oprah's Next Chapter in 2012. "On some level it stung and on some level I was not surprised," she said. "When people show you who they are, believe them. I carry that [mantra] with me a lot. It has served me well."

It was the New York Fashion Week fight heard 'round the world when Nicki and Cardi got into a heated altercation at the Harper's Bazaar Icon party. The following month, Cardi opened up about the catalyst for the fight with Nicki.

"For a while now she's been taking a lot of shots at me," Cardi said in W magazine's Art Issue. "I spoke to her twice before, and we came to an understanding. But she kept it going."

The real spark of the fight came when Cardi saw that Nicki had allegedly liked and then unliked a tweet about Cardi's parenting skills, which Nicki has denied.

"I was going to make millions off my Bruno Mars tour, and I sacrificed that to stay with my daughter," Cardi continued. "I love my daughter. I'm a good-ass f--king mom. So for somebody that don't have a child to like that comment? So many people want to say that party wasn't the time or the place, but I'm not going to catch another artist in the grocery store or down the block."

Tension between Kanye and Taylor first started in 2009, when the "Stronger" rapper took the stage during her acceptance speech at the MTV Video Music Awards. Years later, the two would make up and even become friends, but that came to an end in 2016 after the release of his song "Famous," in which he name-checks the "End Game" singer.

In February 2025, one day before the Grammys, Kanye updated his Instagram to follow only Taylor. He added no further comment, and his fellow musician did not respond publicly to the move.

Carey and J.Lo's supposed feud started when the Queen of Christmas was asked to give her opinion on several singers during a 2003 German TV interview. When asked her opinion on Lopez, she replied, "I don't know her."

Pochettino is due to speak later on Friday

Today’s fixtures | Follow us on TikTok | Mail David

Mauricio Pochettino’s switch from the US men’s national team to Manchester United has been confirmed. Pochettino will guide the US through a pair of Concacaf Nations League matches on Saturday and Tuesday before joining United, for whom his first game will come at Liverpool next Sunday.

The former Chelsea, Tottenham and Southampton manager has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal to replace Michael Carrick, who was sacked on Thursday after leading United to their worst start to a season in four decades.

Cheers Dom. That seems a fair summation of my plans. I’ll start with some Poch…

Right, I shall hand back to David Tindall who will no doubt provide much more United/Pochettino chat, with the occasional post about something else.

Valérien Ismaël has been appointed as Le Havre coach until the end of the season, with the club sitting rock bottom in the Ligue 1 standings.

The 51-year-old former defender, who was hired as a replacement for Didier Digard, will face a huge task to keep Le Havre in the French top tier. Still winless in Ligue 1, Le Havre have two points from 10 matches.

The much-traveled Ismaël has coached teams in Germany, Greece, Austria, Turkey and England, and was most recently at Blackburn. Le Havre said in a statement yesterday that he has handled “emergency situations” in the past, “which could prove very useful in the coming weeks.” AP

Will Carlos Baleba become a key man for United under Pochettino? Much has been made of the Argentinian’s desire to see his teams run, run, and then run some more. In the space of one season at Chelsea, Pochettino improved their running stats.

Baleba looks to be the only current United midfielder with the legs to cover large spaces. Pochettino often prefers a 4-2-3-1, so surely it stands to reason that the former Brighton player will fit in as one of two deep-lying midfielders? Kobbie Mainoo would appear to be the ideal partner for Baleba – and we know Pochettino likes to promote young homegrown talent. What that means for summer signings Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, it remains to be seen. But the news that Bruno Fernandes probably won’t sign a new contract, could mean a shift in the structure of United’s midfield.

Santos was loaned out by Chelsea to Nottingham Forest and Strasbourg during Pochettino’s sole campaign at Stamford Bridge. United may well look to recruit more hard-running midfielders in January or the summer to suit Pochettino’s preferences.

Just watching Carrick’s end-of-season speech on the Old Trafford turf from May, after a 3-2 win over Nottingham Forest.

I suspect he won’t be repeating his praise of the United playing staff, but that connection with the Stretford End is most certainly evident.

Japan head coach Hajime Moriyasu will step down next week, the country’s football association revealed today, cutting short his tenure in the wake of the 2027 Asian Cup’s postponement.

Moriyasu, Japan’s longest-serving coach, was originally set to lead the team at the Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia in January before handing the reins to current Under-23 boss Go Oiwa.

But the Asian Football Confederation announced last week that the tournament would be pushed back to December 2027 due to “exceptional circumstances” in the region, following Houthi attacks on the host country.

That left Moriyasu in limbo, with Japan Football Association (JFA) chiefs last week declining to clarify when the coaching handover would take place.

They said that Japan’s friendlies in Singapore against Brazil on Saturday and Paraguay on Tuesday would be Moriyasu’s last games in charge. AFP

Reports are already emerging suggesting Pochettino will bring Jesús Pérez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jiménez, Sebastiano Pochettino (his son) and Sílvia Tuyà with him to Manchester United. Coaching squad, assemble!

Wow, that’s quite the emotional and heartfelt message from Carrick, speaking directly to the United supporters. That’s a bond that will not be broken, despite the events of the past few months.

He may not have been up to the job, but Carrick remained classy and dignified until the end.

The former head coach has taken to Instagram to address United fans and his departure from the club.

double quotation markDear United fans, I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love. There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I am incredibly grateful.

With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United you need to understand exactly what that means. It’s different to anywhere else.

Ultimately you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time …

I want to say a big thank you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special rare breed …

I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies. I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing … would be to turn the other way. That means more than a win or two …

I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change. I’ll always be proud to have played my part and I’ll always want the very best for it.

I’ll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on.

Pochettino’s first day of work at Carrington will be on Wednesday, if he’s recovered from the jet lag in time.

Just to mark your card, Pochettino is due to speak to the media at 2.15pm (GMT) today in a press conference to preview the USA’s clash with Haiti.

I’m not sure there will be many questions about the makeup of Haiti’s defence. Man United media squad, assemble!

There’s a general consensus in the emails below – and among most Manchester United fans right now – that the owners above Pochettino have made things even trickier for the incoming boss at Old Trafford.

Reader Jeff Sax, however, lies the blame in a slightly different direction. This is what he says on email:

double quotation markPeople should stop blaming the owners. Management and players are responsible... if the management were not so bad maybe there would be better players.

And the players are not being professional in the way they are playing. Nothing to do with ownership.

Emails! Lots of emails! Lots of emails about Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United …

Darren Winter: “We all know that Pochettino is wedded to a basic 4-2-3-1, as were Carrick and Ten Hag, and the current United squad is apparently set up to play that way. But we also know that formations and tactics are cyclical. You would think that the next big team who changes the formation and nullifies 4-2-3-1 with something new will be the team leading the charge (cough Brighton cough), with others working out how to stop or adapt to the new formation.

“That got me thinking about Ruben Amorim. I wonder if that’s what United thought they were doing with hiring a 3-4-2-1 manager? But the problem with that theory is that it gives Ineos a lot of credit for football knowledge they don’t appear to have. So I don’t know, what do you think?”

Paul Simpson: “It seems like the best in class hierarchy at Manchester United are up to their old tricks. A new manager was needed in the summer and as a fan i can fully understand the pull of appointing Carrick after the job he did last season. But Pochettino was coming out of contract after the World Cup so why was he not considered then? I guess it was so they could wait and pay the £10m or so compensation once he had signed a new contract plus whatever they need to pay Carrick for sacking him. It’s decisions like these that show why Ratcliffe pays Wilcox and Berrada the big bucks.”

Pochettino’s confirmation as Manchester United’s new head coach ends a run of near-misses that date back a decade.

He was linked with the post as far back as 2016, also coming close to being appointed in 2018, 2021 and 2022. He has long had an admirer in Sir Alex Ferguson, who praised Pochettino in a 2016 interview when the Argentinian’s Spurs team were approaching their apex.

“You never see him ruffled and the way his team play is a testimony to the work he is doing.

“The most important thing for English football is how many English and young players are in his team. He understands the advantage of playing young people. They won’t let you down and they have been fantastic.”

United’s own statement describes Pochettino as the club’s new ‘head coach’ and reveals he will begin work on 18 November, with “Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the U.S. Men’s National Team”.

Pochettino’s long-time assistants are Jesus Perez and Miguel D’Agostino, as well as goalkeeping coach Antonio Jimenez.

Here’s Pochettino’s statement on his departure from the USMNT:

double quotation markThe opportunity to represent the USA crest was one of the greatest honours of my career. We are so grateful to the players for their commitment, to the fans for their belief, and to the federation for always supporting our staff and creating the opportunities to impact the culture of soccer in this great country.

We want to thank Cindy Parlow Cone, JT Batson and Dan Helfrich for their partnership and incredible working relationships throughout our time here. There is tremendous talent in the US player pool from the youth teams through to the senior team, and it’s one of the reasons we have so much belief for the future of US Soccer. You will always have a special place in our hearts, and we will be supporting the teams whenever they step on the field.

Mauricio Pochettino’s switch from the US men’s national team to Manchester United has been confirmed. Pochettino will guide the US through a pair of Concacaf Nations League matches on Saturday and Tuesday before joining United, for whom his first game will come at Liverpool next Sunday.

The former Chelsea, Tottenham and Southampton manager has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal to replace Michael Carrick, who was sacked on Thursday after leading United to their worst start to a season in four decades.

It’s going to be fascinating whether Pochettino is labelled a ‘head coach’ or a ‘manager’ when United confirm his appointment. We will soon see I suppose.

Here’s another email from Krishna, who I think messaged my colleague David earlier on. It’s a list of problems for Pochettino:

double quotation markHello Dominic. An unwilling captain, [a] chaotic board, non-existent management team, insufficient and disorganised recruiting, a completely frustrated fanbase and an owner who does not just care …

Clearly the United job still has some allure, Krishna. Pochettino has coveted it for a long, long time.

There was a bit of a shock in the Nations League last night: Italy beat France 3-1 after going 1-0 down early on.

Are the Azzurri on their way back under Roberto Mancini? It’s probably too soon to tell, but this was a positive, as France suffered their first defeat under Zinedine Zidane.

Let’s pivot to other matters for a short while … Andy Robertson will equal Scotland’s men’s appearance record if and when he takes the field against North Macedonia tonight. And although the legendary left-back is matching Kenny Dalglish’s Scotland cap record, he insists he’s a way off King Kenny in terms of footballing legacy and reputation.

Scotland also badly need a win to take the pressure off Sébastien Pocognoli, who isn’t having things easy in charge of the Tartan Army. He’s still looking for his first home win as Scotland head coach, this his third attempt.

Pochettino was viewed as having a very distinct philosophy at Tottenham: pressing, fast attacks, narrow wingers etc. These quotes show perhaps he is willing to go away from that, depending on the players at his disposal:

double quotation markI need to adapt to my roster, my squad, and not to think about myself. [My job is] not to coach the squad for myself. I need to coach the team for the team, for the players, not for what I think is good for me. I need to provide the best tools to perform with the characteristics that I have in my squad.

I think much of the chatter around Pochettino, rightly or wrongly, still centres on his (excellent) Tottenham tenure. This interview from earlier this year gives more of an insight into the modern day Poch, how he’s changed and adapted from those years at Spurs.

The PSG-Chelsea-USA run perhaps isn’t the most convincing, but there is important context around all those jobs.

Thanks David. With frost still on the ground in my particular part of south Manchester, the heating is very much on.

Speaking of heat and Manchester, back to Mauricio Pochettino …

Time to test the grey matter as you down a cuppa – and WFHers ponder whether to put the heating on. Plenty of football in this week’s quiz. While you mull which Manchester United boss has spent the longest in the job since Fergie left, I’ll hand the reins to Dominic Booth.

What do our readers think of Michael Carrick’s sacking. A variety of views here…

After several decades of hurt, the world’s favourite sport may finally be getting its artistic due, writes Emma John. In related news, I was in Afflecks Palace in Manchester on Wednesday, admiring some of Stan Chow’s football pop art. Plenty of Christmas present potential there although I’ll also point you to The Guardian Bookshop.

Kane’s lead at the top of the England all-time top scorers chart is ridiculous! Just eight more before he brings up the century. For so long, trying to beat Sir Bobby Charlton’s tally of 49 seemed a massive ask. Fair play to the presumably very fashion-conscious Vivian Woodward for that goals per game ratio.

On email, krishnamoorthy v has been checking his diary.

double quotation markGood morning David. If Poch can’t see the omen of Friday the 13th as his day of appointment, well...

Barney Ronay was at Wembley on Thursday night to celebrate Happy Harry Kane day.

“And as the teams lined up there was a surprise appearance from the real star of this stage, the Ballon d’Or itself, wreathed in event glamour and star-flash. Kane drew the ballon from its stone in Arthurian fashion, then held it a little sheepishly in one hand. Prince William walked out and gave him a massive framed shirt, which seemed weird in the moment, like the chief area sales manager presenting the prize from the Christmas raffle. Has Prince William ever been asked to carry anything before?”

Here’s David Hytner’s report of England’s 2-1 win over Croatia in the Nations League last night. Comes complete with photo of Harry Kane in classic penalty-taking pose.

Arsenal are struggling domestically but they dug out a fine result away to Barcelona in the Women’s Champions League last night. The result left Renée Slegers’ side fourth in the table. Remember, the top four in the 18-team group phase qualify automatically for the quarter-finals. Here’s Suzanne Wrack’s report.

The Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has rejected a second offer of a new contract at Old Trafford but the club are confident of getting the midfielder to commit his future to Old Trafford. The 32-year-old’s current deal runs until the end of the season but United have the option to trigger a further year.

If United elect not to utilise that clause, Fernandes would be allowed to speak to clubs abroad in January. The Portuguese has previously had interest from Saudi Arabia and Galatasaray but chose to stay.

Fernandes won the PFA player of the year award last season after helping United to third in the league with a record-breaking 21 assists, but his form has dipped. He also took aim at Carrick’s tactics after United’s defeat by Como in the Champions League, in the weeks before the manager was sacked.

Here’s Will Unwin again on how Pochettino can reignite Manchester United. Simples.

Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be appointed as the new Manchester United head coach later today. The Argentinian will leave his role with the United States to sign a two-and-a-half year contract at Old Trafford as Michael Carrick’s replacement.

Carrick and his backroom staff were dismissed on Thursday, with Pochettino expected to bring his trusted lieutenants from previous roles with him.

It will cost United £7m in compensation to secure the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss.

A Poch timeline for you. The official announcement is expected later today but Pochettino won’t arrive at the club until next Wednesday. Here’s how the next 10 days look:

Friday 13 November: United are set to confirm his appointment.

Saturday 14 November: He takes charge of the USA in the first leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti in Miami (9.30pm UK time).

Tuesday 17 November: He leads the USA for the last time, in the second leg against Haiti in Cincinnati (midnight UK time).

Wednesday 18 November: He flies to Manchester to meet his new bosses.

Thursday 19 November: He takes his first training session with the players.

Sunday 22 November: His first game in charge is Liverpool away at Anfield (4.30pm). Gulp!

Ahead of Mauricio Pochettino’s unveiling at Manchester United, Andrew Beasley crunches the numbers to look at the Argentine’s possible impact.

An elite manager? The stats say yes: only the five “big beasts” of Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola have better points-per-game averages than Pochettino.

Jack Grealish has issued a public apology to Everton fans after he made his comeback in a behind-closed-doors match with Derby. Grealish has missed four matches and not played for the Toffees since 17 October following a breach of club discipline.

Boss David Moyes has been reluctant to discuss any finer details and the club only confirmed the 31-year-old former England winger was “not match-fit” ahead of a trip to Newcastle on 2 November but Grealish featured in a friendly at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday in the strongest suggestion yet that a line has been drawn over the issue.

“Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training,” Grealish wrote on his Instagram story.

“I want to apologise to the fans and everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks. I love playing for this club and can’t wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt. See you all soon.”

Grealish spent the first half of the 2025-26 campaign on loan at Everton before injury curtailed his spell on Merseyside, but he returned on another temporary deal on transfer deadline day. (Press Association)

Good morning! Harry Kane scores for England and more managerial chaos at Manchester United. Yep, some things never change.

Kane’s penalty, on his record 126th appearance for the Three Lions, secured England’s 2-1 victory over Croatia in the Nations League on Thursday night. Earlier in the day, Michael Carrick had been sacked by Manchester United, paving the way for Mauricio Pochettino to take over the reins at Old Trafford.

We’ll have reaction to those big events, women’s Champions League and Nations League updates plus news of an apology from Jack Grealish to Everton. In other words, lots to talk about and dissect!

#823. BBC to show Dover v Leicester and Salisbury v Blackpool

Leicester City will travel to Crabble, the home of Dover Athletic of National League South

Non-league clubs Dover Athletic and Salisbury will stage the BBC's two chosen FA Cup second-round ties next month.

National League South side Dover welcome former Premier League and FA Cup winners Leicester City to Crabble on Saturday, 5 December (17:15 GMT, BBC Two/iPlayer).

Another sixth-tier side, Salisbury, will host Blackpool, winners of one of the most memorable finals of all time in 1953, at the Raymond McEnhill Stadium the following day (Sunday 6 December, 12:15 GMT, BBC Two/iPlayer).

Dover reached the second round courtesy of a 2-0 home win over National League side Wealdstone and are seeking to reach round three for just the third time in their history, having lost against Huddersfield in 2011 and at home to Premier League outfit Crystal Palace in 2015.

The Foxes - who lost on their first four FA Cup final appearances before Youri Tielemans' goal secured a 1-0 win over Chelsea in the 2021 final - now play in League One after back-to-back relegations and overcame Oxford City of National League North 4-2 in the first round.

Salisbury are yet to concede a goal in their three ties this season and thrashed Sholing 6-0 to reach round two for the first time since the club was reformed in 2015.

Seventh-tier sides Wimborne Town and Plymouth Parkway will also see their home ties against League One Bradford City and League Two Barnet, respectively, televised among the eight selected for live coverage across the weekend.

All clubs featured in live television broadcasts will receive Â£60,000 while the winning and losing clubs in the second round will receive Â£79,500 and Â£21,200 respectively from the competition prize fund.

The third round draw will take place before the televised tie between Guiseley and Notts County at 19:30 GMT on Monday, 7 December.

A comprehensive highlights programme will cover the weekend's action on Sunday, 6 December at 17:10 GMT (BBC Two/iPlayer).

All of the second round's goals will be available to view across BBC digital platforms including the BBC Sport website and app.

While rivals announce increasingly expensive smart telescopes, ZWO’s new Seestar S30 Plus makes galaxy and nebula photography surprisingly affordable.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

As rival makers announce increasingly ambitious smart telescopes, ZWO has taken a different approach. Its new Seestar S30 Plus launched today and is available for $474 from Seestar’s website and Amazon, just in time for Christmas. Better still, we’ve been using it for a month and can bring you a first look.

Announced a few months after the flagship Seestar S50 Pro and replacing the now-discontinued Seestar S30, the new Seestar S30 Plus retains its 30mm aperture and compact chassis, but upgrades to four-element apochromatic optics with extra-low dispersion (ED) glass and two 3.7-megapixel cameras.

It has a 1.2-inch (30 mm) aperture, two 3.7 MP cameras and four-element apochromatic optics bundled into a compact build.

Both produce 1,440 x 2,560-pixel images, while a much-improved 43.5-degree wide-angle camera can capture the Milky Way, constellations, star trails and nightscapes. Built-in filters, a mosaic mode and equatorial (EQ) tracking add considerable deep-sky astrophotography potential.

For a telescope weighing just 3.64 lbs (1.65 kg), it’s impressive. It easily fits into a camera bag and could happily live on a bookshelf.

I’ve already photographed the Andromeda Galaxy (M31), the Pleiades (M45), the Dumbbell Nebula (M27) and the North America Nebula (NGC 7000). The results are excellent for such a small instrument, especially when imaging nebulas with its built-in dual-band filter, which helps reduce light pollution.

The Seestar app adds new in-app post-processing options, so you don’t have to mess around with any of that — though you can also export everything as lossless FITS files. The S30 Plus also includes a magnetic solar filter, enabling you to indulge in solar photography safely.

With Dwarflab’s $1,299 Draco (3.5-inch/90mm aperture) recently landed in stores and Vaonis’ own $4,990 Atlas (3.1-inch/80mm aperture) not available until 2027, ZWO’s decision to offer an upgraded entry-level smart telescope that buyers can get their hands on right now looks particularly smart.

With ZWO's pattern of delivering cheaper smart telescopes without sacrificing on quality, the Seestar S30 Plus could be one of Christmas 2026’s best gifts for anyone interested in astronomy — and maybe that’s the point of it. Either way, first impressions are good. A full review is coming tomorrow, so check back at Space.com to find out our full thoughts and testing.

#820. Who makes your Northern Ireland XI against Ukraine?

Northern Ireland have a number of options to pick from against Ukraine, who they beat 3-0 in the first fixture

After an impressive quadruple-header to kick off the Nations League, Northern Ireland are back in action and it's time for you to be the boss.

Michael O'Neill's young side did not concede a goal as away victories over Georgia and Ukraine were joined by two goalless draws at home to Hungary and the Georgians, which leave Northern Ireland top of League B2 after four matches.

Now, they will look to finish the job and earn promotion to League A as Ukraine visit Belfast on Saturday, before a trip to Hungary on Tuesday to close out the group.

But who would you pick if you were in charge of Northern Ireland? Weigh up some of the key selection dilemmas before having your say.

NI can draw on strong club form in key window

Birthdays and broken lamps - at home with the Charles brothers

Of the 54 teams in the Nations League, Northern Ireland are the only side yet to concede a goal after four rounds of matches.

It's all the more impressive when you consider O'Neill is without two Premier League level defenders, in the form of Liverpool's Conor Bradley, a long-term absentee, and Daniel Ballard, who was injured in the first match of the campaign in Georgia in September.

O'Neill has a plethora of options, both at the heart of defence and out wide.

At centre-back, youngsters Tom Atcheson and Ruairi McConville impressed in the quadruple-header, while O'Neill could also utilise the experience of Paddy McNair or Ciaron Brown.

There are also several options at right-back, with Trai Hume, the in-form Terry Devlin and Brodie Spencer - who can also play at left-back along with Justin Devenny - all available.

In goal, first-choice Pierce Charles has fresh competition in the shape of Manchester United stopper Dermot Mee.

Who would you pick to keep the run of clean sheets going?

Watch on BBC iPlayer and BBC Two NI from19:15 GMT; Listen on BBC Sounds and BBC Radio Ulster; Watch, listen, live text and clips on BBC Sport app & website

Trai Hume has often been deployed as a right winger by Sunderland this season

Trai Hume has become something of a Swiss army knife option for both Northern Ireland and at Sunderland with his versatility.

Usually a right-back, Hume has often been utilised further forward on the right wing by Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris this season.

For Northern Ireland, the 24-year-old has played right across the defensive line when called upon.

With Conor Bradley fit and on the right flank, Hume would often feature as the right of three centre-backs, but he has also been deployed in both full-back positions.

Then, in October, he started in the centre of midfield against Ukraine and did not look out of place with a composed performance in a 3-0 win.

His versatility can only be a positive for Northern Ireland, but where would you play him to get the best out of both player and team?

Finding the back of the net has long been an issue for Northern Ireland, and despite the huge promise of this young team, they do still lack an out-and-out goalscorer.

Jamie Donley has been tasked with leading the line in recent matches, and he has been in good form at club level for Luton Town, albeit in a different role to the one his fills at international level.

His Luton team-mate Callum Marshall is another attacking option, and he can also be used out wide.

Josh Magennis is more of a target man option as he closes in on a century of Northern Ireland caps, while, at the other end of the experience scale, Braiden Graham is on the fringes of the first team with Everton and Eoin Kenny is untested having played just one Championship fixture since joining Portsmouth from Dundalk.

Who would you pick to lead the line against Ukraine on Saturday?

#819. Nicola Peltz Beckham Addresses "Mean" Body Shamers

Nicola Peltz Beckham—who married Brooklyn Peltz Beckham in 2022—chimed in after a fan hit back at body shamers commenting on her appearance in new photos.

Nicola Peltz Beckham is abs-solutely blocking out the noise.

After the Bates Model actress showed off her bare stomach in a selfie, she addressed body shamers commenting on her appearance, while also expressing her gratitude toward supportive fans.

In a Nov. 11 Instagram post, Nicola—who has been married to Brooklyn Peltz Beckham since 2022—shared photos of herself posing in a mirror wearing blue scrubs after an oxygenating cosmetic procedure, with the 31-year-old lifting up her shirt to reveal her flat stomach.

She captioned the post, “hyperbaric chic post facial.”

After a handful of commenters made critical remarks about the Last Airbender star’s looks, one came to her defense to shut down the haters.

“Stop body shaming her and other ppl,” the user wrote. “Are you all perfect?”

The comment didn’t go unnoticed by Nicola, who replied to the fan, “thank you. some people are actually so mean.”

The heartfelt exchange continued as the commenter wrote back, “your [sic] welcome sweetheart. I'm so sick of ppl and there [sic] opinions of others. I'm overweight and I struggle with it do to my health. You are beautiful. I adore you and Brooklyn.”

The Transformers: Age of Extinction star once again thanked the user for their “kind” words.

“I read them and it means a lot to me,” she added. “You’re so beautiful, you’re perfect.”

This isn’t the first time Nicola and Brooklyn have faced body shamers head-on.

Over the summer, an online user made a negative remark about her body in the comments section of one of her husband’s Instagram posts.

And David Beckham and Victoria Beckham’s eldest son didn’t hesitate to defend his wife.

David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025

David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class.

The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract.

He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield.

Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023.

His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas.

David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth Â£128m

He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey".

Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time."

Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility.

Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Womenâs World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019.

"To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram.

The Curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of Nazca as thoroughly as possible before drilling.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

NASA's Curiosity Mars rover is sizing up its next dig site on the Red Planet.

The Curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of the Mars site, informally named "Nazca," as thoroughly as possible before drilling into it.

Curiosity snapped the close-up image on Oct. 18, 2026, using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI). The image shows multiple roughly disk-shaped potential crystal formations at the rover's next drill target.

MAHLI is located on the turret at the end of the rover's robotic arm. It uses an onboard focusing process to make a composite of images of the same target acquired at different positions to focus on multiple features in a single image.

Scientists theorize that the "discs and needles" texture takes its characteristic shape as crystals, or "crystal forms," grow.

The relatively large sizes of the crystal forms at "Nazca" may provide clues about the temperatures at which they grew, as well as information about the abundance of salts and fluids in the area at the time. Complicating this picture, however, is the fact that mineral crystals can be replaced by other minerals after their original crystallization. The new minerals are known as "pseudomorphs," because they have the same shape as the original minerals but not the same composition or molecular structure.

The Curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of Nazca — which shares its name with an ancient South American civilization that's famous for the large designs it etched into the rock and dirt — before drilling begins. The NASA researchers will then be able to compare the deeper composition to the surface-level composition.

Robert Lea is a science journalist in the U.K. whose articles have been published in Physics World, New Scientist, Astronomy Magazine, All About Space, Newsweek and ZME Science. #814. How big a problem is central defence for Pocognoli?

Luke Graham (left) is being tipped for his first Scotland start - on the night Andy Robertson (right) could move level as the most-capped men's international

On Andy Robertson's night, it's difficult to not peek across the rest of the Scotland defensive line and worry.

The left-back will be lauded - whether he likes it or not - as he earns his 102nd cap, equalling Kenny Dalglish's men's record, against North Macedonia on Friday.

The captain is calling for it to be the King's night as much as his, and while the pair of Liverpool greats can have - and laugh - that out between them, the grace period for a giggle for Sebastien Pocognoli is petering out.

After an underwhelming opening camp, the head coach is in desperate need of a first home win - which he is hoping will come against the only side he's been victorious against in his opening four games.

The starting back three from that night in Skopje - Stephen Welsh, Scott McKenna and Luis Binks - are all out injured, forcing the Belgian to dig deep into the pool of central defenders, where he has pulled out a pair of names from the past in an attempt to arrest the porousness that plagued his debut international window.

Forgotten men Ryan Porteous and David Bates - the latter who last played international football seven years ago - join established but recent red card receiver Jack Hendry, and handful-of Scotland-minutes man Luke Graham as the centre-back quartet - but how much of a problem area is it already proving to be for Pocognoli?

Nations League: Scotland v North Macedonia

In comparison to the embarrassment of riches the head coach has in midfield and, more sparingly, in the forward areas, the heart of the back line is a bit bare.

Whoever slots alongside Tottenham Hotspur's Robertson - whether in Pocognoli's preferred back three, which could see Kieran Tierney shift in on the left side, or flat four - it's unlikely the combined caps haul of his centre-back buddies will come nearly close to his century plus.

The last of Los Angeles FCâs Porteous' 13 came against Greece in March 2025, while Bates picked up four under Alex McLeish six years before that.

Saudi Arabia-based Hendry is closing in on the half-century, while Celticâs Tierney has surpassed it. Graham got a matter of minutes in North Macedonia after McKenna was dismissed.

Bates was playing in Germany with Hamburg when he faced Albania, Israel, Kazakhstan and San Marino and, after stints at a couple of clubs in Belgium, he's found himself with newly promoted albeit impressive Turkish Super Lig side Amedspor.

"There are a lot of players who are not available for the defensive line, but [David's] not there for nothing," Pocognoli said at Hampden Park on Thursday.

"He's there because he's performing well in Turkey with a team third in the rankings, in a tough competition."

Managed by Besnik Hasi - who played and managed in the Belgian's homeland - the head coach added: "I know the coach there as well, so I know he's also demanding a lot to the players.

"I can imagine the spirit in which he trains every day and I think for this camp, his experience can help some aspects on the pitch."

No excuses as Pocognoli seeks first Hampden victory

The latter qualities were seen as shortcomings of his predecessor, Steve Clarke, but stability in defence was a trademark of Clarke's tenure.

It's imperative Pocognoli picks up that mantle in his search for his first win at Hampden.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

A robot just played Tinkertoys in space, assembling the first satellite structure ever made without a human touching the controls.

The DARPA-funded project saw a robotic "truss builder" create a reflective antenna using Kapton film, composite fiber tubes and aluminum joints. The implications are huge for future missions, potentially opening up new possibilities to build — or fix — satellites in the final frontier.

"This is the first time that a structure has been autonomously constructed in space," Sergio Pellegrino, an aerospace and civil engineering professor at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), said in a statement on Nov. 5.

The need for such spacecraft will likely rise substantially in the future, as companies assemble giant megaconstellations for cell-phone communications, AI compute and other purposes. Indeed, the ball is already rolling on such ambitious projects, generating enough hype for space startups around the globe to raise a record $20.8 billion in the third quarter of 2026 alone.

Anything that launches aboard a rocket is limited by the size of that vehicle's fairing — the nose cone that protects payloads during their ride to space. In space, however, the ability to stretch out is practically infinite — after taking into account, of course, engineering and financing constraints.

Assembling structures robotically off Earth could therefore be revolutionary, advocates say. And the recent milestone was a step in that direction.

"This work could be useful not only for astronomy and astrophysics, but also for communications and other areas, such as building very large solar arrays for space solar power," said Pellegrino, who's team leader of the truss-building project, a Caltech demonstration mission called Autonomous In-Space Tensioned Reflector Assembly (ASTRA).

ASTRA built a 1.4-meter-wide (4.5-foot) structure in orbit. That's an impressive achievement, but it just scratches the surface of what DARPA wants to accomplish via a program it calls Novel Orbital and Moon Manufacturing, Materials, and Mass-efficient Design, or NOM4D for short.

"NOM4D's objective is to enable efficient, scalable construction of very large structures in space," NOM4D Program Manager Andrew Detor said in a Nov. 5 DARPA statement.

"By 'very large,' I mean hundreds of meters or kilometers in scale. Nothing approaching that scale can be achieved today," Detor added.

ASTRA was a demonstration, allowing researchers to check boxes and identify obstacles before shooting for a bigger goal. And the team did run into issues — specifically, time limitations, which prevented them from building additional sections of the antenna. Still, the researchers were able to prove out the third phase of a larger DARPA project.

Pellegrino's team completed the two previous phases — defining the mission and testing the hardware in a lab — before shipping the ASTRA payload to the spaceflight company Momentus, Inc. for integration into its Vigoride 7 space tug. Vigoride 7 launched on March 30, along with many other payloads, aboard SpaceX's Transporter-16 rideshare mission.

ASTRA flew with two prebuilt sections of a truss, a robotic "manipulator" and parts to make the rest of the truss in space. In brief communication windows totaling 15 minutes a day, engineers sent up commands and checked in on the robot's progress as it picked up things, readied them in the right spot, and performed construction on an assembly plate.

The team overcame many "little surprises" on the way but were not able to finish the entire truss in time. Still, Pellegrino framed the effort as a success.

"Developing a payload of this complexity on such a short timeline was an enormous undertaking for our small team," he said.

Looking into the future, he is hopeful that robots will be able to build larger telescope mirrors for observatories to peer deeper into space, as well as more advanced structures for radio telescopes to listen for distant signals.

NOM4D is also supporting a project from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, but that one will take place at the International Space Station, focusing on how to harden carbon tubes in orbit.

Elizabeth Howell (she/her), Ph.D., was a staff writer in the spaceflight channel between 2022 and 2024 specializing in Canadian space news. She was contributing writer for Space.com for 10 years from 2012 to 2024. Elizabeth's reporting includes multiple exclusives with the White House, leading world coverage about a lost-and-found space tomato on the International Space Station, witnessing five human spaceflight launches on two continents, flying parabolic, working inside a spacesuit, and participating in a simulated Mars mission. Her latest book, "Why Am I Taller?" (ECW Press, 2022) is co-written with astronaut Dave Williams.

#811. Missing Israel games 'stressful' for captain Collins

Collins is back for the final two Nations League games after missing the first four with a calf injury

Republic of Ireland captain Nathan Collins said he felt he left his team-mates "on their own" after missing the two controversial Nations League games against Israel in the last international window through injury.

Collins was sidelined for the four-game window in September and October with a calf problem and had to watch on as the Irish lost 1-0 away to Kosovo, beat Israel 3-0 in Debrecen and then draw 2-2 with Austria at home and 1-1 with Israel again in Serbia.

The first game against Israel in Hungary looked in doubt the previous day when training was delayed as players took a vote on whether to play - amid protests over the Israel-Gaza war - with goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu making himself unavailable for selection.

Back in the squad and speaking before Saturday's game away to Austria, the Brentford defender reflected on his personal disappointment at not being around to support his team-mates as captain during a testing time.

"It was probably more stressful away from it than it might have been in it," Collins said.

"I could only see what I could see online and it made it really tough. I didn't feel like I was afraid, but I felt I left the lads there on their own not being there, not being involved."

O'Shea proud of how team-mates handled Israel games

Republic of Ireland sit third in Group B3 and need two big performances in their last two games, against Austria in Linz and home to Kosovo on Tuesday, to have any chance of topping the group and earning promotion to League A.

Despite the challenges the Israel fixtures presented in the last window, Collins believes Heimir Hallgrimsson's squad are stronger coming out the other side of it and are now relishing the focus coming back to matters on the pitch.

"I just think everyone feels very comfortable around each other. I don't think anyone is shying away, I don't think anyone feels uncomfortable in the group," he continued.

"I just think everyone's really bonded well, there's a different feel to it. If anybody experienced what they went through, I think that's extremely normal.

"I think we will all go through a brick wall for each other. I can only keep emphasising that we're ready to go.

"I think we're excited to go and we want another game of football."

Head coach Hallgrimsson added that Seamus Coleman, who has been in the 24-man squad in a "hybrid" role, will not be considered for selection against Austria.

However, with Liam Scales, Jayson Molumby, Conor Coventry, Adam Idah and Ryan Manning all one yellow card away from suspension, the Icelander did not rule out the prospect of the 38-year-old featuring against Kosovo on Tuesday.

"No, we didn't expect to include him in the squad today," he said.

"On Tuesday, we don't know the situation. We can maybe answer that before that game or after this game. We have five players on a yellow."

Group leaders Austria are missing a number of key players for Saturday's game at Raiffeisen Arena through injury.

Nottingham Forest's Xaver Schlager and Hoffenheim's Alexander Prass, who scored in the draw in Dublin, are the latest to be ruled out.

Manager Ralf Rangnick is already without David Alaba, Maximilian Wober, Nikolas Veratschnig, Paul Wanner, Patrick Wimmer, Florian Grillitsch, Carney Chukwuemeka and Marco Grull for this window.
